newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Labuan offshore banks' deposits up 79 pct.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Labuan offshore banks' deposits up 79 pct.

text.p: The governing authority for Malaysia's offshore financial centre on Labuan island said deposits of banks registered with them rose by 79 percent in 1996 over the previous year.
The Labuan Offshore Financial Services Authority (LOFSA) on Wednesday announced the banks' deposits were at $4.31 billion at the end of 1996 against $2.41 billion a year before.
It said in its annual report for 1996 that loan outstandings of the 52 offshore banks operating at Labuan grew by 42.8 percent to $11.96 billion in 1996 over the previous year.
"Although 71 percent of loans at the end of 1996 were still for residents (Malaysians), it was significantly lower than the percentage at the end of 1995 (83.7 percent)," LOFSA said.
Similarly, residents' share of the total deposits at 63.7 percent at the end of 1996 was much lower than 78.7 percent at the end of the previous year, it said.
LOFSA said borrowings from their respective head offices and other branches accounted for 51.8 percent of funding for the offshore banks. Deposits accounted for another 25.8 percent of the resources.
It said the 52 banks' pre-tax profit in 1996 rose by 73.2 percent to $132.5 million.
